# application

```go
import "github.com/ntlaletsi70/blanketops-environments/pkg/buildtrigger/application"
```

This file owns BackendSelector for the BuildTrigger domain — the routing layer that maps a resolved trigger source to the correct evaluation provider.

Selection is pure: no side effects, no validation, no policy. The domain layer is responsible for validating the trigger source before ForTrigger is called. GitHub is the fallback for unrecognised sources.

This file owns the Mapper for the BuildTrigger domain — the pure translation layer between the resolved BuildTrigger contract and the domain.BuildTrigger type consumed by the application service and provider layer.

The Mapper is copy\-only: no time.Now\(\), no ID generation, no inference. All fields originate from the resolved spec. If the resolver provides it, the Mapper copies it; if the resolver omits it, it is absent in the domain model.

Panics on nil input — a nil ResolvedBuildTrigger indicates a resolver bug and must surface loudly rather than silently producing an empty domain model.

This file owns BuildTriggerService — the application service that orchestrates BuildTrigger evaluation.

The pipeline is intentionally minimal: map, evaluate, write. The service does not make admission decisions itself — that belongs to the Provider. It does not dispatch BuildRuns — that belongs to the build domain after acceptance. It only sequences the three steps and ensures the BuildTrigger CR always reflects the outcome.

<a name="BackendSelector"></a>
## type BackendSelector

BackendSelector routes a BuildTrigger to the Provider responsible for evaluating it. Selection is driven by the trigger source — one provider per source kind.

```go
type BackendSelector struct {
    GitHub api.Provider
    Manual api.Provider
}
```

<a name="BackendSelector.ForTrigger"></a>
### func \(\*BackendSelector\) ForTrigger

```go
func (b *BackendSelector) ForTrigger(trigger domain.BuildTrigger) api.Provider
```

ForTrigger returns the Provider that should evaluate the given BuildTrigger. Falls back to GitHub for unrecognised sources — the domain layer validates the source before this is called.

NewBuildTriggerService constructs a BuildTriggerService with the required collaborators. Provider is a single instance — BackendSelector routes to the correct provider before construction if multiple sources are supported.

<a name="BuildTriggerService.Evaluate"></a>
### func \(\*BuildTriggerService\) Evaluate

```go
func (s *BuildTriggerService) Evaluate(ctx context.Context, resolved *buildtriggerResolution.ResolvedBuildTrigger) error
```

Evaluate maps the resolved trigger to a domain model, delegates admission to the provider, then writes the decision back to the BuildTrigger CR. Status is always written — even when evaluation fails — so the CR reflects the latest outcome.
